title: A two-stage analysis of a series of trials
text: Twenty trials, six varieties, three four blocks per trial, lost plots. trial-level covariate z1 shifts trial mean.
code: set.seed(20260920)  n_var <- 6L n_trial <- 20L trials <- sprintf("t%02d", seq_len(n_trial))  alpha <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = n_var) z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n_trial * 4L), n_trial, 4L) colnames(z) <- paste0("z", 1:4) trial_mean <- 4 + 1.2 * z[, "z1"] + stats::rnorm(n_trial, 0, 0.35)  plots <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_trial), function(i) {   n_block <- sample(3:4, 1L)   d <- expand.grid(     variety = factor(paste0("v", seq_len(n_var))),     block = factor(paste0("b", seq_len(n_block)))   )   d <- d[-sample.int(nrow(d), max(1L, floor(0.08 * nrow(d)))), ]   b <- stats::rnorm(n_block, 0, 0.3)   d$yield <- trial_mean[i] + alpha[as.integer(d$variety)] +     b[as.integer(d$block)] + stats::rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.45)   d$trial <- trials[i]   d }))  head(plots) #>   variety block    yield trial #> 1      v1    b1 4.031727   t01 #> 2      v2    b1 5.211888   t01 #> 3      v3    b1 4.944964   t01 #> 4      v4    b1 5.703127   t01 #> 5      v5    b1 6.137920   t01 #> 6      v6    b1 6.376713   t01

title: A two-stage analysis of a series of trials
text: yield ~ 0 + variety gives one mean per variety, random = ~block accounts blocks. v squared standard error mean, varies trials.
code: stage1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(trials, function(tr) {   dt <- plots[plots$trial == tr, ]   dt$variety <- droplevels(dt$variety)   fit <- flexybayes(     yield ~ 0 + variety,     random = ~block,     data = dt,     backend = "inla",     verbose = FALSE   )   est <- tidy(fit)   data.frame(     trial = tr,     variety = sub("^variety", "", est$term),     ybar = est$estimate,     v = est$std.error^2,     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }))  stage1$trial <- factor(stage1$trial) stage1$variety <- factor(stage1$variety) stage1 <- cbind(stage1, z[match(stage1$trial, trials), ])  rnd(head(stage1, 4)) #>   trial variety  ybar     v    z1     z2     z3    z4 #> 1   t01      v1 4.464 0.328 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365 #> 2   t01      v2 5.353 0.407 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365 #> 3   t01      v3 5.491 0.328 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365 #> 4   t01      v4 5.640 0.328 1.946 -0.898 -0.659 0.365 round(range(stage1$v), 3) #> [1] 0.083 0.902

title: A two-stage analysis of a series of trials
text: means one trial share block effects, errors correlated. vcov() stage-one fit gives covariance, together trials give block-diagonal matrix one row per mean. Passed known_variance, matrix replaces variances: row ii row jj covariance σ2[=j]+Kij\sigma^2 [= j] + K_{ij}. matrix fitted INLA , brms stops known_variance_not_supported.
code: blocks <- lapply(trials, function(tr) {   dt <- plots[plots$trial == tr, ]   dt$variety <- droplevels(dt$variety)   fit <- flexybayes(     yield ~ 0 + variety,     random = ~block,     data = dt,     backend = "inla",     verbose = FALSE   )   v <- vcov(fit)   rownames(v) <- colnames(v) <- paste(tr, sub("^variety", "", rownames(v)))   v }) K <- matrix(0, nrow(stage1), nrow(stage1)) key <- paste(stage1$trial, stage1$variety) for (v in blocks) {   at <- match(rownames(v), key)   K[at, at] <- v }  base_k <- flexybayes(   ybar ~ variety,   random = ~trial,   data = stage1,   known_variance = K,   backend = "inla",   verbose = FALSE )  rnd(data.frame(   term = names(coef(base)),   variances_only = coef(base),   full_covariance = coef(base_k) )) #>                    term variances_only full_covariance #> (Intercept) (Intercept)          2.864           2.835 #> varietyv2     varietyv2          0.342           0.413 #> varietyv3     varietyv3          0.775           0.785 #> varietyv4     varietyv4          1.133           1.175 #> varietyv5     varietyv5          1.637           1.612 #> varietyv6     varietyv6          2.079           2.132

title: Construct a structured-covariance carrier — fb_cov
text: carrier's type selects downstream emit path derives covariance square root. "dense" takes lower Cholesky supplied covariance. "chol" uses supplied factor directly. "precision" inverts via Cholesky precision matrix. "blocks" assembles block-diagonal covariance list per-block matrices. "low_rank" pairs rank-K factor registered approximation scheme (reserved v0.4.0, carrier vocabulary active validated, approximate-covariance fit route activates subsequent release). "blocks" carrier one covariance one standard deviation, flexyBayes refuses name engines: brms route blocks carrier, INLA route fit block standard deviation. precision carrier Matrix::bdiag(lapply(blocks, solve)) states covariance INLA, dense carrier block-diagonal matrix states brms. Inside model formula carrier written inline, matrix argument names matrix passed known_matrices, exactly legacy keyword forms . construction-time check light structural probe (shape, lower-triangular pattern, symmetry, block count). full level-aware validation runs fit time grouping factor.

code: fb_refusals() #> flexyBayes refusal registry: 180 reasons #>  #>   [since 0.16.0] aggregate_argument_invalid #>       `aggregate` is not TRUE, FALSE or "auto". #>  #>   [since 0.11.0.9000] aggregated_evidence_unavailable #>       The marginal likelihood of a fit on the aggregated #>       representation. The engine's value omits constants that depend on #>       the data and, under response standardisation, scales by the #>       number of cells instead of the number of rows, so it is not the #>       marginal likelihood of the rows. summary() reports it as not #>       available, naming this reason, instead of printing a number that #>       cannot be compared. #>  #>   [since 0.16.0] aggregation_out_of_scope #>       The aggregated Gaussian route or flexybayes_stream() was given a #>       model outside the aggregation scope: a family or link it does not #>       carry, a smooth, a random slope, a structured random term or a #>       continuous fixed term. The gate's reason is carried in #>       `scope_reason`. #>  #>   [since 0.16.0] aggregation_plan_ineligible #>       `aggregate = TRUE` on a model the aggregation plan cannot #>       compress. The plan's reasons are carried in `reason_codes`. #>  #>   [since 0.11.0.9000] aggregation_residual_prior_not_composed #>       A Gaussian model sent to the aggregated representation, by #>       aggregate = TRUE or by flexybayes_stream(). The aggregated #>       Gaussian route composes the within-cell sum of squares with a #>       fixed gamma prior on the residual precision, so a stated or #>       default residual prior would not be the prior fitted while #>       prior_summary() reported it. Gaussian models are fitted per row. #>       Binomial and Poisson models still aggregate. #>  #>   [since 0.9.2] aggregation_response_incomplete #>       aggregate = TRUE with missing values in the response. The #>       aggregated path compresses rows into per-cell sufficient #>       statistics, which are not defined for a missing response, so the #>       request has no aggregated reading. Untyped before 0.9.2. #>  #>   [since 0.9.2] aggregation_route_unavailable #>       aggregate = TRUE with no aggregated emit route available, either #>       the named backend carries no aggregated path at all, or no #>       aggregated backend resolves for the model, including a family or #>       link flexybayes_stream() does not aggregate. Raised with #>       site-specific messages. Untyped before 0.9.2. #>  #>   [since 0.3.10] approximate_route_not_yet_registered #>       Approximate covariance / dispatch carriers refuse until an #>       approximation scheme is registered (validate_approximation()). #>  #>   [since 0.4.0] approximation_absent #>       validate_approximation(): the low_rank_smooth scheme is #>       registered but no smooth term was routed through the truncation #>       path on this fit. #>  #>   [since 0.4.0] approximation_no_smooth_path #>       s(..., representation = ): the named scheme is registered but has #>       no smooth-basis emit path at this release. #>  #>   [since 0.4.0] approximation_scheme_unknown #>       validate_approximation(): the fit carries no recognised #>       approximation to validate (it is exact). #>  #>   [since 0.4.0] approximation_spec_invalid #>       s(..., representation = ): the representation spec is not a list #>       / fb_approx() carrying a single-string scheme. #>  #>   [since 0.9.0] ar1_residual_not_representable #>       An AR1 process written on the residual side that flexyBayes does #>       not fit: the 1-D and grouped forms, and the separable form for a #>       response other than Gaussian with the identity link. The #>       separable residual on a Gaussian response fits on INLA without a #>       nugget. #>  #>   [since 0.16.0] ar1_residual_with_random_field #>       The nugget-free autoregressive residual together with an #>       autoregressive field on the random side. flexyBayes fits one of #>       the two per model. #>  #>   [since 0.9.0] ar1_spatial_requires_complete_grid #>       A separable ar1(row):ar1(col) spatial term on INLA is emitted as #>       an AR1xAR1 latent field, faithful only with one observation per #>       grid node. The data are an incomplete or replicated grid. #>  #>   [since 0.9.0] ar2_not_representable #>       ar2() parses for the formula catalogue and has no emit path on #>       either active engine. #>  #>   [since 0.9.0] asreml_function_not_recognised #>       A call in a random or residual formula whose function is outside #>       the recognised ASReml vocabulary.
